name: Disguise
summary: The unit stays in plain view but is drawn as something harmless: one of the viewer's own soldiers or vehicles, a unit it chose to copy, or scenery such as a tree. Turrets, base defences and computer-driven units treat it as what it looks like and let it pass, so it can walk through enemy lines. People are fooled only until they notice a tell: a speed or route that doesn't fit, a land vehicle on water, a soldier in the wrong place. The cover ends when it attacks or unloads riders (some versions only flicker when they fire), when a detector or scan unmasks it, or when someone attacks it on purpose. Unlike cloak it is not hidden, and unlike a decoy there is no separate fake; the disguised unit is usually fragile and pays for its cover by avoiding a fair fight.
counterplay: Bring a detector: attack dogs, scout drones, psychic sensors and similar units see through a disguise, and several of them attack the impostor on their own.
Scan the area: a reveal ability or a detector sweep shows which units are real.
Watch for tells: a copy that moves faster or slower than the real thing, a land vehicle out on the water, a soldier who doesn't move with his squad, a tree that blinks when shots come from it.
Attack the suspect on purpose: a direct attack order, or simply shooting it in a shooter, hurts a disguised unit like any other, and most of them are fragile or unarmed.
Check identities: a fake ally can't be given orders and shows its true name when selected (StarCraft II), and a copied player name belongs to someone who is elsewhere (Team Fortress 2).
Use fire or splash: fire still burns a disguised spy as normal (Team Fortress 2), and area damage hits whoever stands in it, real or not.
Keep a guard on key buildings and chokepoints, so whoever slips through still meets someone who checks.

other_examples.note: Instead of attacking, it targets an enemy soldier and takes on that soldier's look; it can even pick dogs or units that don't walk, which careful players then notice. Units of the player it imitates, and that player's allies, mostly leave it alone, though anyone can still order an attack on it, and attack dogs are never fooled. It then walks into enemy buildings for their sabotage effects (see capture-structure).

sources.title: Spy (Red Alert 2), Command & Conquer Wiki

sources.title: Stealth, Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Lists the spy's disguise among the franchise's ways of hiding.

other_examples.note: A tank that looks like a nearby tree whenever it stands still and can keep firing from that look, showing its real shape for a split second with each shot; units it hits don't strike back by reflex. Computer opponents only get a chance to spot it when close, while watchful humans notice the blink or trees that went missing. The disguise makes up for thin armour.

sources.title: Mirage tank (Red Alert 2), Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Its quote box copies the Mirage Tank paragraph of the Red Alert 2 manual.

other_examples.note: A suicide truck that copies the look of any vehicle its owner can see, civilian cars and drones included, or a look that another bomb truck already wears. It keeps its own speed and handling, so attentive players pick it out while it moves, and enemy stealth detection strips the disguise off.

A tiny, short-lived creature released by a flying detector. When it sees the enemy it turns into that side's basic soldier in the enemy's colours, and enemy units stop attacking it by themselves. No detection exposes it: it dies only to a deliberate attack or when its timer runs out. Opponents find it by clicking it (it takes no orders and shows its real name) or by noticing it has no selection ring when they drag-select their army. Players use it to tag along with the enemy army and scout it.

Takes the look of any soldier, friendly or enemy, at any distance, then walks into buildings to sabotage them or pays for a bribe that converts nearby enemy ground units and ships, which ends the cover and leaves it briefly unable to move. Burst Drones, attack dogs and war bears see through it; it can also pose as a friendly unit to confuse an enemy assault, much as the Sudden Transport does.

shooter_analogues.note: The Spy picks any class of either team; after a short puff of team-coloured smoke he looks like that class and borrows a real player's name, health readout and loadout, while his own team sees him in a paper mask. Enemy sentry guns ignore him. Attacking with anything except the sapper, taking the intelligence or dying ends it. Tells include a speed that doesn't match the class, a name whose owner is standing elsewhere, impossible loadouts and voice lines the real player never said; fire still burns him as normal. A kill from behind with one particular knife makes him take on the victim's look at once.

sources.title: Disguise Kit, Official Team Fortress Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: Taking a guard's or worker's outfit opens areas that are otherwise off limits and lets 47 openly carry tools that fit the role. Certain characters, such as supervisors, bodyguards and people who know the team, see through particular outfits, and in several games guards wearing the same uniform grow suspicious if he stays close too long.

One team plays random pieces of map scenery and hides for a short head start; the other team hunts them. Props can swap to another random object a limited number of times, freeze in place (even in mid-air) and must whistle at fixed intervals, which gives the hunters a lead; the hunters' stun grenade only tells them a prop is near. Teams swap roles each round.

sources.title: Prop Hunt, Call of Duty Wiki

player_translation.summary: A fragile infiltrator that the enemy team's turrets, bots and HUD read as one of their own, or as scenery. The skill is acting the part: moving like the copy, choosing a route and choosing when to drop the cover, while enemy players learn the tells and check suspects cheaply.
as_user: Press Q on a unit in view to copy its look after a short, visible change-over; with the always-on variant you simply look like each viewer's own basic soldier.
Enemy turrets, drones and computer-driven units ignore you, your marker on their minimap is a friendly one, and enemy players see a teammate's name over your head.
You keep your own speed and hitbox, so the cover holds best when you move like the thing you copied and avoid close looks.
Firing, using an ability, unloading riders or being hit ends the cover (the prop variant only flickers when you fire). You pick the moment, so your first shot or sabotage lands before anyone reacts.
A detector or a scan near you unmasks you for the whole enemy team. The unit is cheap and fragile, so being found usually means a quick respawn rather than a long fight.
as_target: The impostor looks like a teammate or a prop. The tells are there on purpose: its name belongs to a teammate your minimap shows somewhere else, it moves at the wrong speed, or it never answers pings.
You can shoot anything at any time. A hit on a disguised enemy breaks the disguise at once, so checking a suspect costs a moment and a little ammo.
Detectors and scan abilities unmask it for your whole team with a loud reveal cue and a minimap marker.
If it reaches a structure or your back line, the usual answers apply: guard, shoot, or follow it.
teammates: Pair the disguise with a strike: the disguised player walks in, opens with a sabotage (capture-structure) or a surprise shot, and the team pushes in behind.
A disguised transport carries a squad past the turrets and unloads deep in enemy lines; unloading ends the cover.
A disguised scout follows the enemy army and pings what it sees, so the team knows when and where the push comes.
Defenders bring a detector or keep a scan ready, and call out suspects with pings; a team that leaves its turrets to watch the door gets surprised.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse; left mouse fires the unit's weapon, if it has one, and firing ends the cover.
Q (signature): copy the look of the unit under the cursor; the change takes a moment and shows a puff of smoke to anyone watching. Q again while disguised drops it on purpose.
Always-on variant: no key; the disguise comes back a few seconds after your last attack or the last hit you took.
Prop variant: stand still for a moment to become a prop; moving ends it.
Enemies need no special key: shooting a suspect, a detector unit or a scan ability reveals it. The pattern uses one counted key (Q), within the T1 budget.
feedback: The disguised player sees their real unit with a mask outline and a banner naming the current disguise, so they always know what the enemy sees.
Teammates see the disguised player in team colour with a mask icon; spectators and the kill feed always show the real unit.
Breaking the disguise plays a sharp sound and a clear shed effect (smoke or a ripple) for everyone nearby, and puts a short-lived 'impostor' marker on the enemy minimap.
Tells stay readable from above: the copy keeps the player's own speed, a land vehicle copy on water leaves a hover wake, and a copied name can be checked against the minimap.
Detector range is drawn as a ring for the detector's team.
changes_from_rts: In the RTS the disguise mainly fools automatic targeting, and only humans see through it. In a team shooter nearly everyone looking is human, so it fools the HUD layer (names, colours, minimap markers) and leaves visual tells instead of being perfect.
RTS spies are unarmed and spent on one building. A player unit needs a payoff after the walk-in (a sabotage, a surprise attack, a carried squad) and a respawn.
The changeling can't be detected at all, which works against bots but would be hopeless against people; here detectors and scans always work.
If the game has no friendly fire, shooting a 'teammate' is a free check. That is the intended counter, so any hit ends the disguise rather than hiding the damage.
Copies are limited to units of the same class and roughly the same size, so the silhouette stays honest; the RA3 transport posing as a grounded aircraft would mislead too much from above.
Turrets and bots ignoring the impostor stays from the RTS original; it is the part that still works when the enemy players are people.

team_play.notes: The disguised player mostly sets things up for others: a scout who shadows the enemy army, a carrier that delivers a squad, a saboteur who opens a base for the push. The other team needs a detector pick or a scan, and players who check and call out suspects.

notes: Each client must receive only what its team should see: the server sends the disguise's model, colour, name and minimap marker to the enemy team and the real data to the owner's team, so a modified client can't read the truth.
All automatic targeting (turrets, drones, bots, aim assist) must respect the disguise, and detectors and scans must override it.
The copy needs a model, animations and sounds for every unit it may copy; limiting copies to one class and size keeps the content manageable.
Clear rules for what ends it (attacking, abilities, unloading, being hit, a detector in range) and when it may be put on again.
The prop variant needs a list of props per map that fit the unit's size, and a rule for when the unit counts as standing still.
A perfect disguise among human players does nothing (everyone checks everyone) or everything (nobody can tell); tune it through the tells and through how cheap a check is.
A strong weapon fired from disguise wins fights before anyone can react; keep disguise on fragile or lightly armed units, or have the first shot reveal the shooter a moment before it lands.
Disguise combined with a self-destruct or a sabotage can wipe a group or a base with no answer but a detector, so detectors must be easy to get.
A disguised player waiting at a spawn point is spawn camping; spawn areas should unmask enemies.
Players must never mistake a real teammate for an impostor after a reveal, so the break cue must be loud and last a moment.
Names, colours and minimap markers are faked on purpose, which erodes trust in the HUD; keep at least one honest tell, such as a copied name whose owner shows elsewhere on the minimap.
Spectators, replays and the kill feed must show the truth, or they become confusing.
Prop disguises on cluttered maps can be invisible from above; keep props readable in size and give them a flicker or sound tell.

variants.name: Copy a target
variants.summary: Pick a unit in view, enemy or friendly, and take its look after a short visible change-over; you keep your own speed and handling, which is the tell.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 2 and 3 spies, Red Alert 3 Sudden Transport, Generals bomb truck, Team Fortress 2 Spy

variants.name: Look like their own
variants.summary: Always on: each enemy sees you as one of their own basic soldiers. After you attack or are hit, the disguise comes back by itself a few seconds later.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 1 spy, StarCraft II changeling

variants.name: Prop when still
variants.summary: Standing still turns you into a piece of scenery, a tree or a crate for instance; firing makes you flicker for a moment, and moving ends it.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 2 Mirage Tank, Call of Duty Prop Hunt

variants.name: Disguised carrier
variants.summary: A transport copies another vehicle while its riders stay hidden inside; letting anyone out ends the disguise.

variants.name: Take the victim's face
variants.summary: A kill from behind gives you the victim's look at once, with no change-over smoke, so you can keep walking through their lines.

variants.name: Wolf in the column
variants.summary: A disguised vehicle that drives into the enemy group and then blows itself up.

adds_strengths.why: Turrets, bots and careless players let it walk through enemy lines, so it chooses where the fight starts.

adds_weaknesses.why: The cover ends when it attacks or is hit, and once found it is usually fragile and poorly armed.

counters.why: Automatic turrets and devices don't fire at what looks like a friend.
Base defences can't see through the disguise, so it slips past them.

countered_by.why: Detectors unmask it for their whole team, and a found infiltrator has little to fight back with.
A scan over the area shows which units are real.
Fire burns a disguised unit like any other, and the burning gives it away.

open_questions: Does Shamble Frontlines have friendly fire? Without it, shooting a 'teammate' is a free check, so the disguise must end on any hit; with it, a check costs something.
Should copies be limited to the same class and size (the proposal here), or may a unit copy anything on the map, as the RA3 transport can?
Should enemy players' name tags lie, or only models and colours? Lying names are stronger but erode trust in the HUD.
Can a disguised unit capture objectives? Team Fortress 2 bars a Spy disguised as an enemy from capturing points; the proposal is to follow that.

shooter_fit.reason: Team Fortress 2's Spy shows it works in a team shooter, and a top-down view makes tells such as speed and routes easy to read. It needs honest tells and cheap checks, or it frustrates.
